Install 1password-cli on Omarchy

The 1Password CLI (the `op` command) lets you fetch and manage vault items, inject secrets into environment variables, and provision shells with credentials, all without opening the desktop app. It is aimed at developers and admins who want to script secret retrieval, wire secrets into CI pipelines, or manage vaults, users, and service accounts from the command line.

  1. Open a terminal.
  2. Run the install command:
    omarchy pkg add 1password-cli
  3. Check it landed. Pacman should list version 2.41.0-1:
    pacman -Qi 1password-cli

Open and use 1password-cli

1password-cli has no window of its own: it is a command-line tool, library or system component. To see the commands it added to your PATH:

pacman -Ql 1password-cli | grep /usr/bin/

1password-cli requirements and compatibility

  • a 1Password account (paid subscription) to authenticate against
  • network access to reach 1Password's servers

Pricing and license

Free to use (the CLI binary itself is free; it is only useful with a paid 1Password account behind it). License: custom.

Uninstall 1password-cli

omarchy pkg drop 1password-cli

Frequently asked questions

How do I install 1password-cli on Omarchy?

Open a terminal and run omarchy pkg add 1password-cli. The download is 15.3 MB and it takes 47.2 MB once installed. Omarchy pulls in any dependencies automatically.

Is 1password-cli free?

Free to use (the CLI binary itself is free; it is only useful with a paid 1Password account behind it). The package is licensed custom.

How do I uninstall 1password-cli?

Run omarchy pkg drop 1password-cli. It removes the package from your system.

What does 1password-cli depend on?

1password-cli declares no dependencies in the Omarchy package database.

Is 1password-cli a desktop app?

No. 1password-cli has no window of its own; it is a command-line tool, library or system component.

Is 1password-cli in the official Omarchy repo?

Yes. It is published as 1password-cli (version 2.41.0-1) in the official Omarchy package repository. 1Password makes it. Project site: https://app-updates.agilebits.com/product_history/CLI2.
